newsitem.title: NORWAY: FOCUS-Three Norway banks say interest income drops.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Three Norway banks say interest income drops.

text.p: Battling tight interest margins, Norway's Den norske Bank (DnB), Fokus Bank and Union Bank of Norway (UBN) reported lower net interest incomes in nine-month results on Thursday.

But DnB, Norway's largest commercial bank, managed to post a 5.3-percent net profit rise to 2.20 billion crowns ($345 million) from a year ago thanks to cost cuts, writebacks and other income to beat market forecasts. DnB shares finished 1.44 percent higher at 21.10 crowns on the Oslo Bourse.

Fokus and UBN did not fare as well. Fokus, the country's third largest commercial bank, said nine-month net profits fell eight percent to 383 million crowns and attributed the weaker result to narrowing interest margins.
UBN, the country's largest savings bank, said nine-month pre-tax profits fell by four percent to 1.06 billion crowns.

Despite higher lending volume, banks are suffering from lower net interest income, their core business. Analysts attribute the drop in lower net income to the competitive situation in Norway's over-banked financial market and a generally lower risk of new loans.
But Fokus said reduced operating expenses was partly offsetting losses from the tight interest margin.
Fokus' operating expenses were trimmed to 620 million crowns from 649 million in the previous nine-month period.
"This shows that the bank is able to meet the increased competition by improved effectiveness," a Fokus statement said.
"Both banks (DnB and Fokus) seem to benefit from cost-cutting measures," an Oslo-based financial analyst said. "It is perhaps the most important thing that they have -- the flexibility to cut costs."
However, this was not true for UBN, which also blamed higher costs for the lower profits. Total UBN operating expenses increased by more than six percent to 2.04 billion crowns.

And though UBN said the sharp fall in the interest margin over the last two years was now levelling out, with the margin throughout the second and third quarters stabilizing at 3.1 percent, it still forecast pressure on margins to continue.

UBN, known locally as Sparebanken NOR, said net interest income fell to 1.88 billion crowns from 2.09 billion, offset some by total other income rising to 1.13 billion from 947 million crowns, including income from real estate business.
"Taking into account that the year has been characterised by tough competition in the market, this result was very good," UBN group director Tore Knudsen said in a statement.

Fokus' net interest income fell to 689 million crowns from 730 million. Total other operating income fell by three million crowns to 330 million because of reduced real estate exposure and lower contribution from associated companies.
DnB nine-month net interest income fell to 3.17 billion crowns from 3.19 billion in the corresponding 1995 period, but other operating income rose to 2.10 billion from 2.07 billion.

"Efforts devoted to developing new products and creating stable sources of non-interest income have produced good results," DnB group managing director Finn Hvistendahl said in a statement. "This includes the sale of Vital's insurance products through the bank's distribution network."
Wholly-owned subsidiary Vital Forsikring ASA recorded after-tax profits of 214 million crowns, up from 201 million. The insurance firm contributed 106 million to group profits.
Total operating expenses fell to 3.36 billion from 3.50 billion. The operating profit before losses rose to 1.99 billion from 1.73 billion.
